entries.title: Proof you asked for: nine fake balls, and the bug behind them
entries.body:
You said you have never seen that ball on the schematic and asked me to prove the app was inventing things. Here is the proof, drawn straight onto your video: every circle is a ball the app believed in at that instant. Green means it had a name, orange means unnamed.
The app believed in NINE balls strung down the middle of empty felt - I checked the raw pixels, there is nothing there - and it had stuck the label 'cue ball' on the topmost fake one while your REAL cue ball (bottom, next to the blue 2) went unnamed.
Then I asked the detector directly what it saw in that frame. Six balls. All correct. So the fakes were not the eye - they were the memory.
Here is the bug: when you strike a ball it moves about 60 pixels between video frames, but the app only looked about 35 pixels away from where a ball was last seen. So it failed to recognise the ball as the same ball, and started a brand new one - every single frame, all the way down the table. That chain of fakes IS your cue ball's path.
Fixed: the app now widens its search based on how fast the ball is actually moving. Same frame, after the fix: 7 objects instead of 14, and the cue ball is correctly named where it actually sits.
This one sat underneath a lot of what you have been complaining about - missing trails, wrong names, phantom shots.

images.caption: BEFORE: nine phantom balls down empty felt; 'cue' label stranded at the top; your real cue ball (bottom right of the blue 2) unnamed.
AFTER: the phantom chain is gone and the cue ball is correctly identified at its real position.

entries.title: The ghost ball living in your corner pocket
entries.body:
One object was causing a large share of the nonsense: the app was seeing the leather of your bottom-left corner pocket as a ball. Permanently.
That fake ball invented motion, invented shots, and made trails dive off the table toward it.
First fix: near a pocket, a low-confidence sighting is furniture, not a ball. That killed most of it - the app's shot count on the bench dropped from 22 events to 14, with all 10 of your real strokes correctly among them.
But one piece of leather was 'confident' enough to survive. So the second fix uses time instead: a ball that appears in a pocket and NEVER moves for 8 seconds is furniture. A real ball that rolls into the jaw arrives from somewhere, so it still counts.

images.caption: Your orange 5 sits on the felt at 170.5s and is gone by 171.5s - a real pot. The dark shape at the corner is the pocket leather the app had been calling a ball for the entire session.

entries.title: Why the app was missing half your shots
entries.body:
You asked me to watch your 4-minute practice clip and compare it to what the app saw. I did, frame by frame.
The clip contains 10 real strokes. The app had recorded 5 of them, invented 2 shots that never happened (they were you setting balls up by hand), and completely missed 5 - including two clean pots.
It also scored a ball you CAUGHT IN YOUR HAND as a make, because the ball's track vanished and the old logic treated 'vanished' as 'pocketed'.
The most important part: the app's own quality score for this session was a perfect 0.00. Its numbers only check things it knows to check. That's why we now compare every change against what I can actually see in the video.
